key_insight: The paper shows that token merging in diffusion models should be guided by diffusion dynamics, not just text relevance. This lets the model preserve both prompt-aligned foreground details and important background objects while still reducing computation.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of deciding which image tokens can be merged safely during diffusion sampling without hurting generation quality, especially when existing text-based criteria fail to protect semantically important background content.
method: Analyze diffusion dynamics to estimate which tokens are more likely to remain important across denoising steps.
Use this token importance signal to decide which tokens to preserve and which to merge during generation.
Improve efficiency while reducing visual degradation compared with methods that only preserve prompt-aligned foreground regions.
impact: This approach can make diffusion-based image generation faster and cheaper without sacrificing output quality. For practitioners, it offers a more reliable way to accelerate inference while maintaining both foreground fidelity and background coherence.
visual_elements: A diffusion-step timeline showing token importance changing over time
Side-by-side comparison of text-relevance merging vs diffusion-dynamics merging
Color-coded image token map highlighting preserved and merged regions
A speed-quality tradeoff chart showing efficiency gains with minimal degradation
paper_title: Which Tokens to Merge? Diffusion Dynamics for Efficient Image Generation
paper_authors: SeungJu Cha, Ye-Chan Kim, HyunGee Kim, Sungho Koh, Dong-Jin Kim
